comparison_policy.reason: existing Python and Rust baselines do not measure the same execution boundary
allowed_claims: each baseline remains within its own runner-bound regression budget
Rust operations satisfy their direct-kernel workload contract
Python C15 EVPI satisfies its reference-oracle cohort budget

baselines.runner_scope: release-mode cargo bench on the executing Rust runner
baselines.measures: one direct invocation per declared foundational operation after process and compilation setup
baselines.does_not_measure: Python validation, array conversion, PyO3 dispatch, serialization, repeated-sample uncertainty, energy, or a matched Python workload
baselines.claim_limit: contract and regression-budget evidence only; not a cross-language speedup claim

baselines.runner_scope: approved CPython 3.14 Linux and Windows hosted-runner cohorts
baselines.measures: nine repeated forty-iteration NumPy EVPI oracle workloads with deterministic percentile-bootstrap uncertainty
baselines.does_not_measure: the public Python facade, PyO3 dispatch, a direct Rust kernel, macOS, other Python versions, memory, or energy
baselines.claim_limit: cohort-specific upper-bound regression evidence only; not representative Python-versus-Rust timing

required_evidence: identical versioned workload and result digest
public Python facade timing including validation and PyO3 conversion
runner identity, compiler, package versions, memory, and energy availability
Linux, Windows, and macOS evidence before a cross-platform claim
paired_baseline_gate.promotion_rule: a reviewed paired artifact may permit a narrowly scoped overhead or speedup claim; local measurements alone cannot
